title: Manufacturer Mail-In Rebate Rules — Northgate Purchases & Returns
content:
A manufacturer mail-in rebate is paid under Northgate Purchases & Returns only for a purchase on a channel that participates in the mail-in rebate programme, for an item with a mail-in rebate offer on record whose start date to end date period contains the order date.

## Rule 1 — Claim deadline

A rebate is claimed only when the claim is made no later than the channel's rebate claim window, in calendar days after the fulfillment date of the purchase. Days are counted as calendar days, the fulfillment date being day 0; the claim must also be made on or before the offer's own claim deadline, so the earlier of the two dates is the last day to claim, and a claim on that last day is in time. The basis is the purchase's recorded fulfillment date and the offer's recorded claim deadline.

| Hypothetical | Fulfillment date (day 0) | Channel window ends | Offer claim deadline | Last day to claim |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 1 March | 31 March (day 30) | 15 April | 31 March |
| B | 1 March | 31 March (day 30) | 20 March | 20 March |

In case B a claim made on 21 March is too late, although it is inside the channel window.

## Rule 2 — Amount and payment

The rebate is the offer's per-unit rebate for each unit still kept on the sale line, up to the offer's member limit when that limit is not zero, and is paid on a Northgate Shop Card as the programme provides. Hypothetical: an offer of 20.00 per unit with a member limit of 2, on a line of 3 units of which 0 have been refunded, pays 2 units, 40.00.

## Rule 3 — Once per offer

One sale line is paid at most once per offer.

## Rule 4 — Effect on Annual Reward and later returns

Rebates are funded by the manufacturer and do not reduce Annual Reward. A rebated unit returned later is refunded at its sale price minus the rebate already paid on it.
